profile.campus_mw_context: The 128,715-sq. ft. data center in Sterling, VA, offers 11 MW of IT capacity and features robust connectivity options with high bandwidth and high-availability circuits and a number of metro and long-haul networks.

reading.body:
CyrusOne NVA4 in Sterling offers 11 MW of IT capacity across 128,715 square feet. Assuming 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this is roughly 275 racks of compute. The facility emphasizes network connectivity with multiple metro and long-haul circuits available, which addresses data movement constraints for distributed training workloads.

Virginia has 330 mapped data centers, but only 25 publish capacity figures totaling 1,603 MW. This campus ranks 26th among Virginia facilities with published capacity, placing it outside the state's top tier. It represents less than 1% of Virginia's disclosed capacity, making it marginal to the state's aggregate AI infrastructure by that measure.

The facility's modest scale and lack of published power credentials beyond IT load mean it is unlikely to host large-scale training runs or frontier model development. It is positioned for enterprise workloads, specialized compute, or distributed inference where network quality matters more than absolute power density. Whether it matters to AI scaling depends on whether Virginia's true aggregate capacity, hidden in the 305 unmapped or unpublished facilities, includes larger campuses nearby.
